chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “There was never any Prophet who came except with recognition of our right and our superiority over those besides us.”

key_terms.تَفْضِيلِنَا: our being given superiority and precedence
key_terms.حَقِّنَا: our rightful claim and due right

ai.seo_question: Did all Prophets come with recognition of the right and superiority of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that all Prophets came bearing recognition of the right of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام and their superiority over others. It presents this recognition as part of the divinely conveyed truth associated with prophethood and wilayah.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Hameed, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abdul A’ala who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is none from a Prophet<sup>saww</sup> who came except with recognition of our<sup>asws</sup> rights and our<sup>asws</sup> merits over the ones besides us<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘ from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani who has said the following.

“I heard abu Ja‘far (a.s.) say, “By Allah, in the heavens there are seventy lines of angles. Even if all the inhabitant of earth would try to count them they will not be able to count them. All of these angels acknowledge our Wilaya (Leadership with Divine Authority).”
